review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

5:1.sourceText: Μετὰ ταῦτα ἦν ἑορτὴ τῶν Ἰουδαίων, καὶ ἀνέβη Ἰησοῦς εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.
5:1.targetText: Some time later there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

groups.note: Μετὰ ταῦτα "after these things" is rendered Some time later.

5:2.sourceText: Ἔστιν δὲ ἐν τοῖς Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐπὶ τῇ προβατικῇ κολυμβήθρα, ἡ ἐπιλεγομένη Ἑβραϊστὶ Βηθζαθά, πέντε στοὰς ἔχουσα.
5:2.targetText: Now there is in Jerusalem near the Sheep Gate a pool with five covered colonnades, which in Hebrew is called Bethesda.

groups.note: The adjective προβατικῇ "sheep-" is rendered Sheep Gate; the Greek leaves the noun understood.
The article with the participle, "the one called", is rendered which is called.
Same pool, named in a different form in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:3.sourceText: ἐν ταύταις κατέκειτο πλῆθος τῶν ἀσθενούντων, τυφλῶν, χωλῶν, ξηρῶν(, ἐκδεχομένων τὴν τοῦ ὕδατος κίνησιν.
5:3.targetText: On these walkways lay a great number of the sick, the blind, the lame, and the paralyzed.

groups.note: The pronoun ταύταις "these" (the colonnades) is rendered these walkways.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB follows a reading without these words ("waiting for the movement of the water").

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the last item of the list; the Greek list has no conjunction.

5:4.sourceText: ἄγγελος γὰρ κατὰ καιρὸν κατέβαινεν ἐν τῇ κολυμβήθρᾳ καὶ ἐτάρασσε τὸ ὕδωρ· ὁ οὖν πρῶτος ἐμβὰς μετὰ τὴν ταραχὴν τοῦ ὕδατος ὑγιὴς ἐγίνετο, ᾧ δήποτε κατείχετο νοσήματι).

unmappedSource.reason: BSB has no verse 5:4; it follows a reading without this account of an angel stirring the water.

5:5.sourceText: ἦν δέ τις ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖ τριάκοντα καὶ ὀκτὼ ἔτη ἔχων ἐν τῇ ἀσθενείᾳ αὐτοῦ·
5:5.targetText: One man there had been an invalid for thirty-eight years.

groups.note: ἦν … ἔχων "there was … having (spent)" is rendered had been.
ἐν τῇ ἀσθενείᾳ αὐτοῦ "in his illness" is rendered as the noun an invalid.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

5:6.sourceText: τοῦτον ἰδὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς κατακείμενον, καὶ γνοὺς ὅτι πολὺν ἤδη χρόνον ἔχει, λέγει αὐτῷ Θέλεις ὑγιὴς γενέσθαι;
5:6.targetText: When Jesus saw him lying there and realized that he had spent a long time in this condition, He asked him, “Do you want to get well?”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves ἤδη ("already") untranslated.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds where he lay; κατακείμενον means lying.
English supplies the state from 5:5; the Greek says only that he "has" a long time.

5:7.sourceText: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ ὁ ἀσθενῶν Κύριε, ἄνθρωπον οὐκ ἔχω, ἵνα ὅταν ταραχθῇ τὸ ὕδωρ βάλῃ με εἰς τὴν κολυμβήθραν· ἐν ᾧ δὲ ἔρχομαι ἐγὼ, ἄλλος πρὸ ἐμοῦ καταβαίνει.
5:7.targetText: “Sir,” the invalid replied, “I have no one to help me into the pool when the water is stirred. While I am on my way, someone else goes in before me.”

groups.note: βάλῃ "put" is rendered help (me into the pool).
ἐν ᾧ "in the time in which" is rendered While.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves αὐτῷ ("to him") unexpressed.
BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.

5:8.sourceText: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἔγειρε ἆρον τὸν κράβαττόν σου καὶ περιπάτει.
5:8.targetText: Then Jesus told him, “Get up, pick up your mat, and walk.”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a connective; the Greek has none here.

5:9.sourceText: καὶ εὐθέως ἐγένετο ὑγιὴς ὁ ἄνθρωπος, καὶ ἦρεν τὸν κράβαττον αὐτοῦ καὶ περιεπάτει. Ἦν δὲ σάββατον ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ.
5:9.targetText: Immediately the man was made well, and he picked up his mat and began to walk.  Now this happened on the Sabbath day,

groups.note: BSB recasts Ἦν "(it) was" as happened.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse; BSB leaves it untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB renders ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ("on that day") as on the Sabbath day, without that.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject referring to the healing; the Greek says "it was Sabbath on that day".

5:10.sourceText: ἔλεγον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι τῷ τεθεραπευμένῳ Σάββατόν ἐστιν, καὶ οὐκ ἔξεστίν σοι ἆραι τὸν κράβαττον.
5:10.targetText: so the Jews said to the man who had been healed, “This is the Sabbath! It is unlawful for you to carry your mat.”

targetPhrases.text: to the man who had been healed

groups.note: The article with the participle, "the one healed", is rendered the man who had been healed.
οὐκ ἔξεστιν "it is not lawful" is rendered It is unlawful.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence and leaves καί untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with an extra word here, rendered your; N1904 has only the article.

5:11.sourceText: ὃς δὲ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς Ὁ ποιήσας με ὑγιῆ, ἐκεῖνός μοι εἶπεν Ἆρον τὸν κράβαττόν σου καὶ περιπάτει.
5:11.targetText: But he answered, “The man who made me well told me, ‘Pick up your mat and walk.’”

groups.note: The relative ὅς with δέ serves as the pronoun he.
The article with the participle, "the one who made", is rendered The man who made.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves αὐτοῖς ("to them") unexpressed.
BSB leaves the resumptive ἐκεῖνος ("that one") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:12.sourceText: ἠρώτησαν αὐτόν Τίς ἐστιν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ εἰπών σοι Ἆρον καὶ περιπάτει;
5:12.targetText: “Who is this man who told you to pick it up and walk?” they asked.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves αὐτόν ("him") unexpressed after asked.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object; the Greek command has none.

5:13.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἰαθεὶς οὐκ ᾔδει τίς ἐστιν· ὁ γὰρ Ἰησοῦς ἐξένευσεν ὄχλου ὄντος ἐν τῷ τόπῳ.
5:13.targetText: But the man who was healed did not know who it was, for Jesus had slipped away while the crowd was there.

groups.note: The article with the participle, "the one healed", is rendered the man who was healed.
The genitive absolute ὄχλου ὄντος is rendered as a while-clause.
ἐν τῷ τόπῳ "in the place" is rendered there.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:14.sourceText: Μετὰ ταῦτα εὑρίσκει αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Ἴδε ὑγιὴς γέγονας· μηκέτι ἁμάρτανε, ἵνα μὴ χεῖρόν σοί τι γένηται.
5:14.targetText: Afterward, Jesus found the man at the temple and said to him, “See, you have been made well. Stop sinning, or something worse may happen to you.”

groups.note: Μετὰ ταῦτα "after these things" is rendered Afterward.
The pronoun αὐτόν (him) is rendered the man.
γέγονας "you have become" is rendered you have been made.
ἵνα μή "so that … not" is rendered or.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:15.sourceText: ἀπῆλθεν ὁ ἄνθρωπος καὶ εἶπεν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν ὁ ποιήσας αὐτὸν ὑγιῆ.
5:15.targetText: And the man went away and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well.

groups.note: BSB's Greek has a different verb of the same sense here.
The article with the participle, "the one who made", is rendered who had made.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a connective; the Greek has none here.

5:16.sourceText: καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἐδίωκον οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι τὸν Ἰησοῦν, ὅτι ταῦτα ἐποίει ἐν σαββάτῳ.
5:16.targetText: Now because Jesus was doing these things on the Sabbath, the Jews began to persecute Him.

groups.note: διὰ τοῦτο … ὅτι "for this reason … that" is rendered because.
BSB names Jesus earlier in the sentence and renders τὸν Ἰησοῦν here as Him.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject of was doing; the Greek gives it only in the verb.

5:17.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἀπεκρίνατο αὐτοῖς Ὁ Πατήρ μου ἕως ἄρτι ἐργάζεται, κἀγὼ ἐργάζομαι·
5:17.targetText: But Jesus answered them, “To this very day My Father is at His work, and I too am working.”

groups.note: In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he, rendered Jesus; BSB's Greek has an extra word here.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:18.sourceText: διὰ τοῦτο οὖν μᾶλλον ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἀποκτεῖναι, ὅτι οὐ μόνον ἔλυεν τὸ σάββατον, ἀλλὰ καὶ Πατέρα ἴδιον ἔλεγεν τὸν Θεόν, ἴσον ἑαυτὸν ποιῶν τῷ Θεῷ.
5:18.targetText: Because of this, the Jews tried all the harder to kill Him. Not only was He breaking the Sabbath, but He was even calling God His own Father, making Himself equal with God.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective οὖν untranslated.
BSB starts a new sentence instead of rendering ὅτι ("because").
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:19.sourceText: Ἀπεκρίνατο οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐ δύναται ὁ Υἱὸς ποιεῖν ἀφ’ ἑαυτοῦ οὐδὲν, ἂν μή τι βλέπῃ τὸν Πατέρα ποιοῦντα· ἃ γὰρ ἂν ἐκεῖνος ποιῇ, ταῦτα καὶ ὁ Υἱὸς ὁμοίως ποιεῖ.
5:19.targetText: So Jesus replied, “Truly, truly, I tell you, the Son can do nothing by Himself, unless He sees the Father doing it. For whatever the Father does, the Son also does.

groups.note: Ἀπεκρίνατο … καὶ ἔλεγεν "answered and said" is rendered replied.
οὐ … οὐδέν (a double negative) is rendered nothing.
ἂν μή together supply unless; BSB's Greek differs slightly here, with the same sense.
The pronoun ἐκεῖνος "that one" is rendered the Father.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves αὐτοῖς ("to them") unexpressed.
BSB leaves the resumptive ταῦτα ("these things") untranslated.
BSB leaves ὁμοίως ("likewise") untranslated.

5:20.sourceText: ὁ γὰρ Πατὴρ φιλεῖ τὸν Υἱὸν καὶ πάντα δείκνυσιν αὐτῷ ἃ αὐτὸς ποιεῖ, καὶ μείζονα τούτων δείξει αὐτῷ ἔργα, ἵνα ὑμεῖς θαυμάζητε.
5:20.targetText: The Father loves the Son and shows Him all He does. And to your amazement, He will show Him even greater works than these.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.
BSB leaves the relative ἅ ("that") unexpressed in all He does.

5:21.sourceText: ὥσπερ γὰρ ὁ Πατὴρ ἐγείρει τοὺς νεκροὺς καὶ ζωοποιεῖ, οὕτως καὶ ὁ Υἱὸς οὓς θέλει ζωοποιεῖ.
5:21.targetText: For just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whom He wishes.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of gives life; the Greek verb has none.

5:22.sourceText: οὐδὲ γὰρ ὁ Πατὴρ κρίνει οὐδένα, ἀλλὰ τὴν κρίσιν πᾶσαν δέδωκεν τῷ Υἱῷ,
5:22.targetText: Furthermore, the Father judges no one, but has assigned all judgment to the Son,

groups.note: οὐδέ … οὐδένα (a double negative) is rendered no one.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:23.sourceText: ἵνα πάντες τιμῶσι τὸν Υἱὸν καθὼς τιμῶσι τὸν Πατέρα. ὁ μὴ τιμῶν τὸν Υἱὸν οὐ τιμᾷ τὸν Πατέρα τὸν πέμψαντα αὐτόν.
5:23.targetText: so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. Whoever does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent Him.

groups.note: The article with the participle, "the one not honoring", is rendered Whoever does not honor.

5:24.sourceText: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ὁ τὸν λόγον μου ἀκούων καὶ πιστεύων τῷ πέμψαντί με ἔχει ζωὴν αἰώνιον, καὶ εἰς κρίσιν οὐκ ἔρχεται ἀλλὰ μεταβέβηκεν ἐκ τοῦ θανάτου εἰς τὴν ζωήν.
5:24.targetText: Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever hears My word and believes Him who sent Me has eternal life and will not come under judgment. Indeed, he has crossed over from death to life.

groups.note: The article governs both participles: "the one hearing … and believing".

unmappedSource.reason: ὅτι introduces the direct speech and has no English counterpart.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:25.sourceText: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἔρχεται ὥρα καὶ νῦν ἐστιν ὅτε οἱ νεκροὶ ἀκούσουσιν τῆς φωνῆς τοῦ Υἱοῦ τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ οἱ ἀκούσαντες ζήσουσιν.
5:25.targetText: Truly, truly, I tell you, the hour is coming and has now come when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.

unmappedSource.reason: ὅτι introduces the direct speech and has no English counterpart.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:26.sourceText: ὥσπερ γὰρ ὁ Πατὴρ ἔχει ζωὴν ἐν ἑαυτῷ, οὕτως καὶ τῷ Υἱῷ ἔδωκεν ζωὴν ἔχειν ἐν ἑαυτῷ.
5:26.targetText: For as the Father has life in Himself, so also He has granted the Son to have life in Himself.

5:27.sourceText: καὶ ἐξουσίαν ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ κρίσιν ποιεῖν, ὅτι Υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου ἐστίν.
5:27.targetText: And He has given Him authority to execute judgment, because He is the Son of Man.

5:28.sourceText: μὴ θαυμάζετε τοῦτο, ὅτι ἔρχεται ὥρα ἐν ᾗ πάντες οἱ ἐν τοῖς μνημείοις ἀκούσουσιν τῆς φωνῆς αὐτοῦ
5:28.targetText: Do not be amazed at this, for the hour is coming when all who are in their graves will hear His voice

groups.note: ἐν ᾗ "in which" is rendered when.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the verb; the Greek has only the article with the phrase "in the tombs".

5:29.sourceText: καὶ ἐκπορεύσονται οἱ τὰ ἀγαθὰ ποιήσαντες εἰς ἀνάστασιν ζωῆς, οἱ τὰ φαῦλα πράξαντες εἰς ἀνάστασιν κρίσεως.
5:29.targetText: and come out—those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment.

groups.note: The article with the participle, "the ones who did", is rendered those who have done.
The article with the neuter plural adjective makes a noun, rendered good.
The article with the participle, "the ones who practiced", is rendered those who have done.
The article with the neuter plural adjective makes a noun, rendered evil.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with an extra word here; N1904 has no conjunction between the two groups.

5:30.sourceText: Οὐ δύναμαι ἐγὼ ποιεῖν ἀπ’ ἐμαυτοῦ οὐδέν· καθὼς ἀκούω κρίνω, καὶ ἡ κρίσις ἡ ἐμὴ δικαία ἐστίν, ὅτι οὐ ζητῶ τὸ θέλημα τὸ ἐμὸν ἀλλὰ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πέμψαντός με.
5:30.targetText: I can do nothing by Myself; I judge only as I hear. And My judgment is just, because I do not seek My own will, but the will of Him who sent Me.

groups.note: Οὐ … οὐδέν (a double negative) is rendered nothing.
The emphatic attributive ἐμόν "(the) mine" is rendered My own.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds only for emphasis; καθώς means as.

5:31.sourceText: Ἐὰν ἐγὼ μαρτυρῶ περὶ ἐμαυτοῦ, ἡ μαρτυρία μου οὐκ ἔστιν ἀληθής·
5:31.targetText: If I testify about Myself, My testimony is not valid.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:32.sourceText: ἄλλος ἐστὶν ὁ μαρτυρῶν περὶ ἐμοῦ, καὶ οἶδα ὅτι ἀληθής ἐστιν ἡ μαρτυρία ἣν μαρτυρεῖ περὶ ἐμοῦ.
5:32.targetText: There is another who testifies about Me, and I know that His testimony about Me is valid.

groups.note: The relative clause ἣν μαρτυρεῖ "which he testifies" is rendered by the possessive His.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:33.sourceText: ὑμεῖς ἀπεστάλκατε πρὸς Ἰωάνην, καὶ μεμαρτύρηκεν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ·
5:33.targetText: You have sent to John, and he has testified to the truth.

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

5:34.sourceText: ἐγὼ δὲ οὐ παρὰ ἀνθρώπου τὴν μαρτυρίαν λαμβάνω, ἀλλὰ ταῦτα λέγω ἵνα ὑμεῖς σωθῆτε.
5:34.targetText: Even though I do not accept human testimony, I say these things so that you may be saved.

groups.note: παρὰ ἀνθρώπου "from a man" is rendered human.
BSB turns "not … but" into a concessive clause; the contrast of ἀλλά is carried by Even though.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:35.sourceText: ἐκεῖνος ἦν ὁ λύχνος ὁ καιόμενος καὶ φαίνων, ὑμεῖς δὲ ἠθελήσατε ἀγαλλιαθῆναι πρὸς ὥραν ἐν τῷ φωτὶ αὐτοῦ.
5:35.targetText: John was a lamp that burned and gave light, and you were willing for a season to bask in his light.

groups.note: The pronoun ἐκεῖνος "that man" is rendered John.
The article with the participle, "the one burning", is rendered that burned.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:36.sourceText: ἐγὼ δὲ ἔχω τὴν μαρτυρίαν μείζω τοῦ Ἰωάνου· τὰ γὰρ ἔργα ἃ δέδωκέν μοι ὁ Πατὴρ ἵνα τελειώσω αὐτά, αὐτὰ τὰ ἔργα ἃ ποιῶ, μαρτυρεῖ περὶ ἐμοῦ ὅτι ὁ Πατήρ με ἀπέσταλκεν.
5:36.targetText: But I have testimony more substantial than that of John. For the works that the Father has given Me to accomplish—the very works I am doing—testify about Me that the Father has sent Me.

groups.note: Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves the object αὐτά ("them") unexpressed after accomplish.
BSB leaves the relative ἅ ("that") unexpressed in the very works I am doing.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies that (the testimony) for the comparison.

5:37.sourceText: καὶ ὁ πέμψας με Πατὴρ, ἐκεῖνος μεμαρτύρηκεν περὶ ἐμοῦ. οὔτε φωνὴν αὐτοῦ πώποτε ἀκηκόατε οὔτε εἶδος αὐτοῦ ἑωράκατε,
5:37.targetText: And the Father who sent Me has Himself testified about Me. You have never heard His voice nor seen His form,

groups.note: The resumptive ἐκεῖνος "that one" is rendered by the emphatic Himself.
οὔτε … πώποτε "neither … ever" is rendered never.

5:38.sourceText: καὶ τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἔχετε ἐν ὑμῖν μένοντα, ὅτι ὃν ἀπέστειλεν ἐκεῖνος, τούτῳ ὑμεῖς οὐ πιστεύετε.
5:38.targetText: nor does His word abide in you, because you do not believe the One He sent.

groups.note: καί … οὐκ "and … not" is rendered nor.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB recasts "you do not have His word abiding in you" as nor does His word abide in you; ἔχετε ("you have") has no English counterpart.
BSB leaves the relative ὅν ("whom") unexpressed in the One He sent.

5:39.sourceText: ἐραυνᾶτε τὰς γραφάς, ὅτι ὑμεῖς δοκεῖτε ἐν αὐταῖς ζωὴν αἰώνιον ἔχειν· καὶ ἐκεῖναί εἰσιν αἱ μαρτυροῦσαι περὶ ἐμοῦ·
5:39.targetText: You pore over the Scriptures because you presume that by them you possess eternal life. These are the very words that testify about Me,

groups.note: The article with the participle, "the ones testifying", is rendered the words that testify.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence and leaves καί untranslated.

5:40.sourceText: καὶ οὐ θέλετε ἐλθεῖν πρός με ἵνα ζωὴν ἔχητε.
5:40.targetText: yet you refuse to come to Me to have life.

groups.note: οὐ θέλετε "you do not want" is rendered you refuse.

5:41.targetText: I do not accept glory from men,

5:42.sourceText: ἀλλὰ ἔγνωκα ὑμᾶς ὅτι τὴν ἀγάπην τοῦ Θεοῦ οὐκ ἔχετε ἐν ἑαυτοῖς.
5:42.targetText: but I know you, that you do not have the love of God within you.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

5:43.sourceText: ἐγὼ ἐλήλυθα ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Πατρός μου, καὶ οὐ λαμβάνετέ με· ἐὰν ἄλλος ἔλθῃ ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τῷ ἰδίῳ, ἐκεῖνον λήμψεσθε.
5:43.targetText: I have come in My Father’s name, and you have not received Me; but if someone else comes in his own name, you will receive him.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds a connective; the Greek has none here.

5:44.sourceText: πῶς δύνασθε ὑμεῖς πιστεῦσαι, δόξαν παρὰ ἀλλήλων λαμβάνοντες, καὶ τὴν δόξαν τὴν παρὰ τοῦ μόνου Θεοῦ οὐ ζητεῖτε;
5:44.targetText: How can you believe if you accept glory from one another, yet do not seek the glory that comes from the only God?

groups.note: The participle λαμβάνοντες is rendered as an if-clause.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a verb; the Greek has only the article with "from the only God".

5:45.sourceText: μὴ δοκεῖτε ὅτι ἐγὼ κατηγορήσω ὑμῶν πρὸς τὸν Πατέρα· ἔστιν ὁ κατηγορῶν ὑμῶν Μωϋσῆς, εἰς ὃν ὑμεῖς ἠλπίκατε.
5:45.targetText: Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father. Your accuser is Moses, in whom you have put your hope.

groups.note: The article with the participle, "the one accusing", is rendered accuser.

5:46.sourceText: εἰ γὰρ ἐπιστεύετε Μωϋσεῖ, ἐπιστεύετε ἂν ἐμοί· περὶ γὰρ ἐμοῦ ἐκεῖνος ἔγραψεν.
5:46.targetText: If you had believed Moses, you would believe Me, because he wrote about Me.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.

5:47.sourceText: εἰ δὲ τοῖς ἐκείνου γράμμασιν οὐ πιστεύετε, πῶς τοῖς ἐμοῖς ῥήμασιν πιστεύσετε;
5:47.targetText: But since you do not believe what he wrote, how will you believe what I say?”

groups.note: γράμμασιν "writings" is rendered what … wrote.
ῥήμασιν "words" is rendered what … say.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
